title: Establish the governing scaffold and validated implementation backlog
summary: Build the requested repository scaffold from the starter discussions: governing neutral contracts, complete scoped roadmap, ticket schema and coverage, executable repository checks, synthetic lifecycle examples, and a reviewable GitHub change.
in_scope: Governing contracts, source corrections and explicit domain ownership.
Canonical ticket records, human-readable projections, dependency graph and requirement inventory.
Executable validation, regression tests and synthetic Oil/civic/DIAT walkthroughs.
out_of_scope: Implementing every future runtime or research ticket in this bootstrap.
Changing another repository, publishing private data, training identity models or deploying a core system.
implementation: Preserve original notes and add governing documents with a clear precedence and ownership decision.
Create every scoped ticket with concrete acceptance criteria, tests, dependencies and reuse sources.
Implement schema/graph/coverage/projection validation and deterministic synthetic walkthroughs with independently declared expected outputs.
Run negative regression tests, document executed evidence and push a coherent reviewable change.

acceptance.criterion: All scoped requirements map to detailed valid tickets and the dependency graph is complete and acyclic.
acceptance.verification: Run python -m matter validate and independently inspect the coverage and dependency-readiness reports.

acceptance.criterion: The repository can be installed and its documented validation and walkthrough commands execute without live credentials or private data.
acceptance.verification: Install the package, run validation, the unit suite, and all three synthetic walkthroughs; record exact results.

acceptance.criterion: The governing contracts state implemented scaffold limits and keep downstream runtime, semantic qualification and DIAT experiments planned.
acceptance.verification: Review README, source map, contracts and all ticket completion fields against the actual code and executed evidence.

acceptance.criterion: The completed scaffold is committed and available for review on GitHub with source and validation references.
acceptance.verification: Verify the pushed tree and pull request head contain the checked files and that the PR summary distinguishes completed scaffold work from future tickets.

tests: Corrupt ticket fields, dependencies, requirement references and completion evidence must fail validation.
Duplicate/redelivered events, stale pending updates, wrong recovery and direct controls must have the declared behavior.
Malformed classifications and path-traversal ticket IDs must be rejected before lifecycle or filesystem mutation.
risks: A detailed roadmap can be mistaken for completed production behavior unless states and evidence are explicit.
Cross-repository requirements can be lost or accidentally implemented in the neutral core.

reuse.application: Preserve their design rationale while formalizing the clarified contracts and source limitations.

sources: User scaffold request and correction on 2026-10-08.

evidence: 2026-10-08: editable installation, render --check, repository validation, all 39 regression tests and all three synthetic walkthroughs passed; see docs/validation.md.
The 80-ticket, 104-requirement backlog has 271 acceptance criteria, complete coverage, no missing dependencies, no cycles and no phase inversions.
